name: events
description: The event protocol: one row per thing that happened, naming who it happened to, who did it, and what it touched. Written beside the change, never instead of it.

columns.name: type
columns.description: The event name, e.g. CONTRIBUTION_CONFIRM. An open set in legacy — one constant per file under backend/src/event/.
columns.open: Not an enum here. Legacy has around 60 of these as string constants, and the set grows with every feature. Whether gradido2 contracts them as a closed enum or keeps them open decides whether an unknown value on read is an error or a fact.

columns.name: affected_user_id
columns.description: Whose account the event is about.

columns.name: acting_user_id
columns.description: Who caused it. Equal to affected_user_id for an ordinary member action; a moderator or admin id when somebody acted on another's behalf.
columns.note: Migration 0061 wrote 0 into this column for the ADMIN_CONTRIBUTION_UPDATE rows it could not reconstruct. A 0 here points at no user and must not be joined blindly.

columns.name: involved_user_id
columns.description: The third party, where there is one — the recipient of a transfer.

columns.name: amount_gdd4
columns.description: Signed: negative on a send, positive on a receive. Migration 0061 flipped the sign of the existing TRANSACTION_SEND rows to make it so.

notes: Append-only, like transactions: the row is the event. Nothing updates or deletes here, and both implementations must treat an UPDATE or DELETE on this table as a bug.
Six nullable involved_* columns, of which an event fills at most two. It is a wide sparse row rather than a polymorphic reference, and a reader must not assume that exactly one is set.

This is not the log. logging.json describes what both implementations emit to stdout; this table is business history that survives the process. A change that writes one and not the other is incomplete.

Legacy declares no index at all here, and the admin views read it by affected_user_id and by created_at. Whatever gradido2 reads it by needs an index written into this file — see contracts/AGENTS.md, indexes are part of the contract.
Timestamps are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json. Migration 0061 raised created_at to datetime(3), so rows written before it have second precision.
